entries.text: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026, positioning it as a frontier‑level model for software engineering, knowledge work, and scientific tasks.
The model is available through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers.
It supports a 1 million‑token context window and is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens.
Neon achieved a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranking #3 overall and #2 on the Vals Index with 70.9% performance.
It leads on the Agent Arena Index for steerability, ranking #2, and records the lowest fabrication rate in Google’s internal Antigravity tests.
Independent benchmarks place Neon #1 on the Legal Research Bench, Tax Agent Bench, and most finance and accounting tasks on Surge AI, while it scores 73.5% on Chartography for dense chart reading.
The model also matches top scores on Agents' Last Exam v1.1 (75.8%) and tops Zapier’s AutomationBench (56.3%) and Andon Labs' Vending‑Bench 2 ($16,843).
Large language models are increasingly used for complex, multi‑modal workflows, but many struggle with long contexts and reliable step‑by‑step reasoning.
problems: model check: Sources do not mention that many models struggle with long contexts or step‑by‑step reasoning; they only highlight Neon’s capabilities.

Nvidia announced it will stop shipping its H200 AI chips to China following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO last week.
Interim CEO Colette Kress made the statement during the company's earnings call on Tuesday.
The decision ends a controversial arrangement that allowed the chips to be exported through the United States with a 25% tariff.
The H200 chips are built on Nvidia's Hopper architecture and were previously sold to Chinese customers after a special export license was granted in December 2025.
Under Huang, the deal was brokered with President Donald Trump and required the chips to pass through U.S. ports, generating revenue for the U.S. government.
Kress said Nvidia's guidance now excludes any licensed Hopper data‑center products for China, and she gave no further explanation for the halt.
Nvidia's H200 chips are among the most powerful AI accelerators, used by labs for large‑scale model training.

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on Thursday, November 18, 2026, above the previously indicated range of $70 to $78.

entries.text: The company will begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT” and is valued at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
The pricing suggests strong investor interest despite recent market volatility linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure.
The $83 price places Anthropic’s market value at $1.5 trillion, up from $965 billion in May when it raised $65 billion in a private round, but below the $2 trillion target it had set months earlier.
Strategic partners Amazon and Google own nearly 15 % and almost 14 % of the company respectively, dwarfing the stakes of any single venture‑capital backer, none of which hold more than 5 %.
A consortium of tech firms including AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreed to buy $26 billion of non‑voting shares in a private placement alongside the IPO.
Anthropic is a leading AI startup known for its Claude models and has been preparing for an IPO as the AI sector seeks public market validation.
The pricing comes after a period of uncertainty in AI stocks, highlighted by the market reaction to Nvidia’s leadership change, which had shaken confidence in the industry.
The IPO’s success could set a benchmark for other private AI firms, such as OpenAI, which remains privately valued at $1.25 billion and has not announced IPO plans.

Google DeepMind rolled out Genie 4 on 18 November 2026 to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, adding real‑time text and audio editing to Project Genie environments.
The update also introduced a Project Genie agent that guides users through natural‑language conversations to build custom worlds.
Subscribers can publish their creations in a new community gallery for others to explore and remix.
Genie 4 enables users to change weather, add characters, and insert adaptive audio while navigating a world, all triggered by typed prompts.
The earlier Genie 3 model now supports longer sessions, panorama grounding, and linked world sequences, improving continuity across scenes.
The Project Genie agent assists in constructing complex environments through simple dialogue, and the community gallery serves as a shared repository for created worlds.
Project Genie began earlier in 2026 as an experimental prototype that let users generate and explore interactive digital worlds.
Early testers asked for deeper control and easier sharing, prompting the development of Genie 4 and the agent interface.
